summary.en: Build a stack at the list head and release each removed node safely.
summary.bn: লিস্টের head-এ স্ট্যাক বানাও আর সরানো node-এর মেমরি ছেড়ে দাও।

notes: Programs use C17 with explicit bounds and ownership checks.

examples.title: Push at head, then drain
examples.explanationHtml: Nodes leave in the order 36, 24, 12. Each pop saves next before freeing the old head.

examples.title: Accumulate while releasing nodes
examples.explanationHtml: The sum is independent of removal order. No node remains allocated after the loop.

examples.title: Inspect values during a destructive traversal
examples.explanationHtml: Three even values are counted while their nodes are removed.

practice.title: Print reverse input with nodes
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n values -99..99. After the input prompt, print Removed: followed by the pop order. Allocate one node per value and release all nodes.
hints: Insert each new node before the old head.

practice.title: Add popped integers
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n values -99..99. Drain a linked stack and print Result: followed by the sum after the prompt.
hints: Use a separate integer for the popped value.

practice.title: Count positive nodes
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and values -99..99. Print Result: and the number greater than zero after releasing the linked stack. Include the input prompt.
hints: A boolean comparison adds either zero or one.

practice.title: Inspect linked top, then release the chain
practice.statementHtml: Read 0..16 values in -99..99 after their count. Print the size prompt, then Top: with the latest value or Top: empty. Inspect without popping, then release every node.
hints: Read top only after checking for NULL.

quiz.prompt: Which list end supports both stack updates in constant pointer work?
quiz.explanation: The head directly identifies the node to remove and the insertion gap.

quiz.prompt: What should failed malloc do to top?
quiz.explanation: No new node exists to publish.

options: The old object ends its lifetime at free
quiz.explanation: Accessing freed storage is invalid even when bytes appear unchanged.

quiz.prompt: How is an empty linked stack represented?
options: top points to a zero value
The last node points to itself
quiz.explanation: A null head means no live nodes.

quiz.prompt: Which storage cost distinguishes a linked stack from a fixed int array?
options: A four-byte pointer on every C system
quiz.explanation: Pointer size is platform dependent; each node still needs a link.

quiz.prompt: Does no fixed capacity mean push cannot fail?
quiz.explanation: Available memory and allocator behavior still limit growth.

quiz.prompt: For n linked stack nodes, what does complete destruction cost?
quiz.explanation: Every allocated node must be freed once.

quiz.prompt: When a node with value 9 precedes 4, which value does the head read?
After following next from 9 to 4, what value is exposed?
quiz.explanation: The successor becomes the new top.

quiz.prompt: How many links does a one-node linked stack traverse to become empty?
quiz.explanation: Following the singleton next link reaches NULL.

keyPoints.en: The list head is the linked stack top.
keyPoints.bn: লিংকড স্ট্যাকের top হলো লিস্টের head।

keyPoints.en: Allocate before changing the existing head pointer.
keyPoints.bn: বরাদ্দ সফল হওয়ার আগে পুরোনো head বদলাবে না।

keyPoints.en: Pop saves the successor before freeing the old node.
keyPoints.bn: Pop-এ পুরোনো node ছাড়ার আগে পরের node রাখো।

keyPoints.en: A linked stack can fail when allocation fails.
keyPoints.bn: মেমরি বরাদ্দ না হলে লিংকড স্ট্যাকে push ব্যর্থ হয়।

keyPoints.en: Node links add storage and allocation work.
keyPoints.bn: Node-এর link রাখতে বাড়তি মেমরি ও বরাদ্দের কাজ লাগে।

examQuestions.question: Write the node publication steps for linked-stack push after allocation succeeds.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
node->value = value;
node->next = *top;
*top = node;

Check malloc before these lines. The old top stays reachable through next. Link work is constant.

examQuestions.question: A pop frees the head and then reads head->next. Explain the bug and write a safe replacement.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Node *old = *top;
*value = old->value;
*top = old->next;
free(old);

Run these lines only after checking that *top is not NULL. Reading next before free avoids use after free.

examQuestions.question: Write a complete pop helper for Node **top and a valid int output pointer.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
static int pop(Node **top, int *value)
{
    if (*top == NULL) {
        return 0;
    }
    Node *old = *top;
    *value = old->value;
    *top = old->next;
    free(old);
    return 1;
}

The caller supplies valid pointer arguments. Read both fields before free. One removal performs constant link work and releases one allocation.
